scope: Theorem 4.1 (Construction of the residual ideal operator) of the manuscript “Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers” (preprints/Weighted-Dilation-Graphs-Smooth-Shifted-Primes-and-Totient-Fibers-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 011 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 351692885d112277), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix Eid > 0 and a fixed frequency exponent C4 ≥ 0. There are fixed integers m, J0 and a fixed constant C1, depending only on these parameters, ℓ, and the prime-group bounds, with the following property. For every fixed J ≥ J0, there is a family consisting of the raw pattern Cg = ∅ for every g, K0 = 1, and signed comparison patterns satisfying Cg = ∅ (g ∈ S), |Cg| ≤ m (g ∈ B), X ν sup |Kν| ≤ LC1 , such that the symmetrized ideal operator of Section 3 satisfies sup Θ∈R, |ζ|≤LC4 ∥T (Θ)∥2→2 ≤ L−Eid (4.1) for sufficiently large x. The coefficients and the family are independent of Θ and of the individual value of ζ. Their defining parameters are independent of J; J only supplies the available shared slots. The threshold for x may depend on J. More precisely, designate m of the first J slots in each big group as probes, and split the big groups into two blocks. Each comparison frees nonempty sets A and B of designated probes in the respective blocks, and its coefficient has the form −(−1)|A|+|B| KA(DA, XA)KB(DB, XB). (4.2) Here DA, DB are the products of the free labels used to form D, XA is the product of the target labels in A, and XB the product of the input labels in B. These coefficients use no shared labels and none of the last ℓ labels. Each kernel is a finite sum of products of matched log-cell indicators and pairs of Dirichlet characters of conductor bounded by a fixed power of L.
